questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere that had academic courses which interested me and were not offered at KU, and also somewhere with a lifestyle I thought I would enjoy

Additional comments:

questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was a coordinator who emailed all the international students and told us how to register for classes, dates of orientation week, how to get health insurance etc., but most things I did on my own

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, I used a platform called Flatmates

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is definitely a better option than the university housing options and better value for money. It just takes more effort to look on your own and can be tricky to do when you are not living there yet, but certainly doable

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not live in this but from what I saw online and from reading reviews it seemed unimpressive and expensive for what you got

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Exchange students are only able to take certain courses, meaning that not every class listed online is open to exchange students. The academic coordinator sends you a big excel spreadsheet of courses and you select 6-8 which you are interested in on the registration portal and then find out whether or not you are accepted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The academic coordinator was available when you had questions and she always responded quickly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into every class I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure that you do everything as soon as you can to make sure you have the highest chance of getting into the classes that you want because they can fill up if you wait until the last minute. Otherwise it is an easy process

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of my classes were at the MA level across different faculties

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I much preferred the teaching style at University of Sydney. Classes were much more engaging and their was more out of class responsibility. We had several different assignments throughout the semester which contributed to your overall grade instead of a single grade like at KU. I found the teaching style in Sydney to be more interactive and representative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Relations
Food and Water Security
Dynamics of Human Rights Violations

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the International Relations course because it was new and interesting to me and gave me a much better idea of how complex global systems are in relation to my degree (Global Health). The Human Rights course was also really interesting and we had good assignments which allowed us to be autonomous and pick a topic we were interested in while also being critical through course material

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Finding a job definitely allows you to meet more people especially as a masters student. Helps to have some income as well

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There lots of cool road trips to do up an down the coast and just explore Australia in general

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you are a masters student I feel like everyone is fairly established in their life so don't expect to make a ton of friends through university. It is fairly international I just found it easier to meet people outside of university

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pretty laid back but still has a good city energy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Definitely find a part time job at a bar or coffee shop etc. Important to earn some money because Sydney is not cheap but also a really good way to meet people who live in your area
2. Look for your own housing. The university options are not great but they are guaranteed and that is also an easy way to make friends. However a lot of them are bachelors students so if you are getting your masters it is a much younger crowd
3. Apply for the student Opal (transport) card as soon as possible, it will make your public transport costs way cheaper. Also do not expect to bike anywhere, it is not like Copenhagen in that way

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a different environment than Copenhagen but super easy to adjust to. I would just recommend trying to make your own life outside of the university. Live close to the beach if you can, find a cool job, and get out and explore when you're free

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed my classes but I loved the job I had and the people I met through that. That is certainly the thing that made me feel the most settled

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None, it was super easy

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None

questions.answer: Yes
